content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1 (every lever except overtime, both queues) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best available plan but still falls short of the 80% target at a predicted 67.5% for 11:30-13:30.","why":"Payments calls jumped 90% above forecast (213 vs 111.9 at 10:30) because of the P1 UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). Service level fell to 4.7% and 59 calls were abandoned. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43 agents) and handle time is below forecast, so this is a demand problem, not a staffing one. No plan reaches 80% without overtime, and overtime is not allowed today. R1 gets closest: 67.5% overall (payments 60.8%, general 77.9%) against 48.7% if we do nothing. Abandons drop from 11.4% to 7.5%, and the rest of the day improves to 86.6%. It costs ₹1,008. Escalation is required because even this best compliant plan is predicted at 68%, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02).","trade_offs":["Cost vs R2: R2 costs nothing and predicts 64.2% (payments 58.1%) with 8.8% abandons. R1 spends ₹1,008 to gain about 3 points and fewer abandons.","Vs P3 (₹624, 61.8%): R1 costs ₹384 more but adds about 6 points and widens chat deflection and IVR messaging.","Customer impact: R1 relies on IVR outage messages, callbacks and chat deflection, so some customers are redirected rather than answered live. Agents' breaks are also pushed back by 30-45 minutes on both queues.","Other queue: general is protected under R1 at 77.9%, but it still misses 80% because its breaks are delayed and callbacks are added there too."],"watch":"Payments service level and abandons each interval, plus any update on the UPI incident. If the outage runs past 13:30 or payments stays near 60%, the duty manager should decide on wider measures. One option is reconsidering the overtime restriction, since no compliant plan clears the 70% line."}
